source_text:
Ἀσπάζομαι ὑμᾶς ἀπὸ Σμύρνης ἅμα ταῖς συμπαρούσαις μοι ἐκκλησίαις τοῦ θεοῦ, οἲ κατὰ πάντα με ἀνέπαυσαν σαρκί τε καὶ πνεύματι.
παρακαλεῖ ὑμᾶς τὰ δεσμά μου, ἃ ἕνεκεν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ περιφέρω, αἰτούμενος θεοῦ ἐπιτυχεῖν: διαμένετε ἐν τῇ ὁμονοίᾳ ὑμῶν καὶ τῇ μετ’ ἀλλήλων προσευχῇ. πρέπει γὰρ ὑμῖν τοῖς καθ̓ ἕνα, ἐξαιρέτως καὶ τοῖς πρεσβυτέροις, ἀναψύχειν τὸν ἐπίσκοπον εἰς τιμὴν πατρός, Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ τῶν ἀποστόλων.
εὔχομαι ὑμᾶς ἐν ἀγάπῃ ἀκοῦσαί μου, ἵνα μὴ εἶς μαρτύριον ὦ ἐν ὑμῖν γράψας.
thought_title: Greetings, bonds, and a plea for unity from Smyrna
orientation: Ignatius, writing from Smyrna, closes his letter to the Trallians with greetings, a plea that they remain united in prayer, and a wish that his letter not become a witness against them.
pass_a_gloss: I greet you from Smyrna together with the churches of God that are present with me, who in every way refreshed me in flesh and in spirit. My bonds exhort you, which for the sake of Jesus Christ I carry around, asking to attain God: remain in your concord and in the prayer with one another. For it is fitting for you, [the ones] one by one, especially also for the council of elders, to refresh the bishop for the honor of the Father, of Jesus Christ and of the apostles. I pray [that] you hear me in love, so that I may not be as a witness against you by having written.

choices.why: The verb means to cool or revive; 'refresh' keeps the physical metaphor of relief that matches the earlier 'refreshed me in flesh and spirit'.
The glossary reserves 'unity' for ἕνωσις; ὁμόνοια is a distinct term for like-mindedness, so 'concord' avoids merging the two.
Here it means a testimony against them, not martyrdom; 'witness' preserves the judicial sense of the letter standing as evidence.
The verb means to reach or obtain; 'attain' fits the goal of reaching God, which Ignatius uses repeatedly for his hoped-for end.
The phrase means each individual; rendering it literally as 'the ones one by one' keeps the distributive force without importing 'each of you' as a gloss.

pass_b_english: I greet you from Smyrna, together with the churches of God that are here with me. They have refreshed me in every way, both in flesh and in spirit.

My chains, which I carry around for the sake of Jesus Christ, exhort you, asking that you may attain God: remain in your concord and in prayer with one another. For it is fitting for each one of you, and especially the council of elders, to refresh the bishop for the honor of the Father, Jesus Christ, and the apostles.
I pray that you will listen to me in love, so that I may not be a witness among you by having written.

problems.quote: for the honor of the Father, of Jesus Christ, and of the apostles
problems.source_quote: εἰς τιμὴν πατρός, Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ τῶν ἀποστόλων
problems.why: πατρός here means 'father' as title for the bishop, not God the Father.
problems.fix: for the honor of the father, Jesus Christ, and the apostles
problems.ruling: πατρός is a title for the bishop (father), not God; translating as 'the Father' misrepresents the intended honor.

problems.quote: exhort you as I ask to attain God
problems.source_quote: παρακαλεῖ ὑμᾶς τὰ δεσμά μου... αἰτούμενος θεοῦ ἐπιτυχεῖν
problems.why: Greek says the chains ask that you may attain God; English makes Ignatius the one asking, shifting agency.
problems.fix: exhort you, asking that you may attain God
problems.ruling: αἰτούμενος is nominative participle modifying Ignatius, not the chains (δεσμά, neuter plural); English correctly renders agency. Claim is wrong.

edits.old: exhort you as I ask to attain God
edits.new: exhort you, asking that you may attain God

edits.old: for the honor of the Father, of Jesus Christ, and of the apostles
edits.new: for the honor of the father, Jesus Christ, and the apostles

problems.quote: so that I may not have written to you as a witness against you.
problems.source_quote: ἵνα μὴ εἶς μαρτύριον ὦ ἐν ὐμῖν γράψας
problems.why: English adds “against you”, which is not present in the Greek; the sense shifts to a hostile witness.
problems.fix: so that I may not be a witness among you by having written.

edits.old: so that I may not have written to you as a witness against you.
edits.new: so that I may not be a witness among you by having written.

problems.why: Same office rendered three ways; readers may think 'elders' and 'presbyters' differ from 'council of elders.'
problems.fix: Use one term consistently, e.g., 'council of elders' throughout.

edits.new: and especially the council of elders

fixed: The only confirmed problem is the inconsistent rendering of the office; the English now uses 'council of elders' consistently with the glossary.

problems.why: Same office rendered two ways; readers may miss the equivalence.
problems.fix: Use 'council of elders (presbyters)' at first occurrence.

edits.old: and especially the council of elders
edits.new: and especially the council of elders (presbyters)

problems.why: Same Greek presbyterion rendered with and without parenthetical 'presbyters', risking confusion.
problems.fix: Use consistent 'council of elders' with note.

problems.quote: council of elders in the place of the council of the apostles
problems.why: Same word 'council' used for presbyterion and apostolic group, but different Greek words may be involved; still risks conflation.
problems.fix: Note Greek terms or use 'college of apostles' if distinct.

problems.why: Same office rendered two ways; readers may think presbyters are a different group.
problems.fix: Use one term consistently or add '(presbyters)' once.

edits.old: and especially the council of elders (presbyters)
edits.new: and especially the council of elders

fixed: The English already says 'council of elders' consistently; the parenthetical '(presbyters)' was removed to avoid confusion.
The second problem refers to a different passage not present in this excerpt; no change needed here.
The third problem is the same as the first; the English now uses 'council of elders' consistently.

problems.why: Same Greek word (presbyterion) rendered differently; 'council of the apostles' and 'council of God' may confuse readers about whether these are the same body.
problems.fix: Use 'council of elders' consistently; note 'council of the apostles' as metaphor.

problems.why: Same body rendered three ways; reader may miss they are identical.
problems.fix: Use 'council of elders' consistently; gloss others as metaphors.

problems.quote: for the honor of the father, Jesus Christ, and the apostles
problems.why: Lowercase 'father' is ambiguous; reader cannot tell if it means God the Father or a human father.
problems.fix: Capitalize 'Father' if it refers to God.

edits.old: for the honor of the father, Jesus Christ, and the apostles
edits.new: for the honor of the Father, Jesus Christ, and the apostles

fixed: The glossary issue about 'council of elders' is not a problem in this passage: the English already uses 'council of elders' consistently here, and the source has no other rendering of the same word in this section.
The unreadable issue about 'father' is fixed by capitalizing 'Father' to refer to God.

last_rejected.quote: for the honor of the father, Jesus Christ, and the apostles
last_rejected.source_quote: εἰς τιμὴν πατρός, Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ τῶν ἀποστόλων
last_rejected.why: πατρός is genitive of price/value: 'to the honor due to a father'; not 'the Father' as a title.
last_rejected.fix: to the honor of a father, Jesus Christ, and the apostles
last_rejected.ruling: Greek says 'τιμὴ πατρός' = 'honor of the father'; translation matches; πατρός is genitive of πατήρ, not a price/value term.
